requirements.requirement: Configure node1 (VyOS) to route between lan-a and lan-b networks
requirements.summary: node1 eth1 (10.50.10.254/24, lan-a) and eth2 (10.50.20.254/24, lan-b) were configured and committed, with a firewall forward filter (default-drop plus explicit accept rules eth1<->eth2) permitting bidirectional forwarding. Configuration was confirmed via 'show interfaces ethernet'/'show firewall' and persisted across a full reboot of node1.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other directly on any port
requirements.summary: Static routes were added on node2 and node3 pointing to node1 for the peer subnet. Bidirectional ICMP (ping) succeeded both before and after all three node reboots, and bidirectional arbitrary-port TCP traffic (port 12345, not a standard/opened service port) succeeded in both directions via nc, demonstrating the firewall/routing permits traffic on a non-default port rather than only a narrow allow-list.

requirements.requirement: Original source addresses are preserved (no NAT applied)
requirements.summary: tcpdump captured on node3's LAN interface shows ICMP echo request/reply with unmodified source IP 10.50.10.10 (node2's true address) both before and after the node reboots. The committed VyOS firewall configuration shown in evidence contains only forward-filter rules with no source-nat/masquerade rules, consistent with pure routing.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all managed nodes (node1, node2, node3) with pre-restart baseline, disruption, changed boot identity, and recovered service/config/connectivity state
requirements.summary: For each node a pre-reboot boot_id was captured, a reboot was issued, a connection-timeout (node1) or later poll confirmed disruption/reconnection, and a new, different boot_id was observed on reconnect (node1: 5bcff8f9→7451f01f; node2: dfeb3b70→0099ce2e; node3: 28ae5f98→f9645d62), matching the fixed after-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots. Post-reboot state was verified: node1's interface config persisted, node2/node3's static addresses, routes, and end-to-end ping succeeded, and node3's post-reboot tcpdump again showed the unmodified source IP, confirming full functional recovery.

overall_summary: The executor configured node1 (VyOS) as a router between lan-a and lan-b with interface addressing, firewall forward rules, and matching static routes on node2/node3, and directly demonstrated bidirectional ICMP and arbitrary-TCP-port connectivity between node2 and node3 with source addresses preserved (no NAT), confirmed via tcpdump. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed for all three nodes with clear pre/post boot-identity changes, a genuine disruption window, and verified recovery of interface config, routes, and end-to-end connectivity/source-preservation afterward, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. A minor, fully-reverted diagnostic mutation (temporary link-local addresses) and a promptly self-corrected firewall rule error were the only notable deviations, with no residue in the final state.
limitations: Arbitrary-port testing was limited to a single non-standard TCP port (12345) rather than a broad port sweep; 'any port' is inferred from the unrestricted forward-filter rules plus this one successful port test rather than exhaustive port coverage.

Source-address preservation was directly observed only for ICMP traffic via tcpdump; TCP source-IP preservation is inferred from the absence of any NAT/masquerade rules in the committed firewall configuration rather than a packet capture during the TCP tests.

Post-reboot verification for node1 relied on interface-configuration persistence plus a subsequent successful node2→node3 ping through it, rather than a fresh explicit firewall/show-forward-state check after node1's own reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace reviewed chronologically. One bounded troubleshooting mutation was found: temporary link-local IPs (169.254.1.2/24 on node2, 169.254.1.3/24 on node3, cmd-eab61f1fe74947f4 and cmd-a5a6048fe6964548) were added to identify which physical NIC mapped to VyOS eth1/eth2 via ARP/tcpdump; the intended arping tool was missing so the attempt partly failed, but it served a legitimate diagnostic purpose (topology discovery, a prerequisite for correct interface configuration) and was fully reverted (cmd-08639de3081648dc, cmd-3001e77391624e3e). A VyOS firewall commit (cmd-89eae15d1ff0466b) partially failed on invalid 'state established/related enable' syntax, leaving an overly permissive stray rule 5 (unconditional accept) until it was promptly corrected by deletion (cmd-56ff5a5db3db4c7f) — a corrective action, not penalized. All test artifacts (nc listeners/PIDs, tcpdump logs, reboot logs) were cleaned up on all three nodes at the end (cmd-e5940037b9144235, cmd-2a1d5e777a1746d9, cmd-16f370a23a664908), and the lifecycle diff shows no residual unexpected temp files or failed services beyond normal boot-scoped systemd-private directories. No unnecessary or destructive mutations remained in the final state.
